summary: auth login with no flags opens the installed Chrome/Chromium headed in a CLI-owned profile (<data dir>/login-browser), waits for the user to sign in, reads only __Host-instacart_sid plus the optional Same-Day companions over CDP via --remote-debugging-pipe (no DevTools TCP port on macOS/Linux; Windows falls back to a 127.0.0.1 random port; browser target only: Browser.getVersion, Target.getTargets, Storage.getCookies, Browser.close), saves them with the session-cookie expiry and closes the browser; --chrome and --cookies-file stay as fallbacks. Actionable errors: expired/missing session says run auth login, a 429/rate-limit page on a costco.com host aborts with wait 15-30 minutes, keychain/keyring denials from --chrome suggest the browser login or the cURL import. auth status and doctor report the live session verdict (valid member / guest / expired), account type and expiry; auth status exits 4 when the probe shows the session expired.
reason: The user could not sign the CLI in: Chrome Safe Storage rejected his keychain password, the box Chrome profile only held a guest session, and failures gave no next step.
rules_check: cli-printing-press skills/printing-press/references/browser-sniff-capture.md forbids shipping a resident browser / browser sidecar transport for normal commands; a login-only browser that exits after capture matches the sanctioned press-auth companion (docs/solutions/logic-errors/auth-login-chrome-broken-2026-05.md, chromedp-controlled Chrome with a separate user-data-dir) and the dominos-pp-cli auth login precedent (library/food-and-dining/dominos/internal/cli/auth_login.go). Normal commands remain plain HTTP.
markers: Costco is rate-limiting sign-in (HTTP 429 from signin.costco.com)
validated_outcome: go build/vet green; go test ./internal/cli green, including headless Chrome against a local TLS fake sign-in page (guest cookie, /signin, callback that sets the member cookie): only __Host-instacart_sid and ahoy_visit are captured (an unrelated cookie is not), expiry is recorded, the browser's DevTools port closes after capture, a 429 sign-in page aborts with the wait message, a guest-only session times out with a Sign in via Costco.com hint, and auth login end to end saves the session and auth status reports the expiry. auth status / doctor tests use local stubs (member, guest, HTTP 401); no test reaches the real site. Review round: pipe client unit-tested against a fake browser; real headless Chrome login tests pass over the pipe and assert no DevToolsActivePort file, a 0700 profile and the marker; reset tests cover unmarked, forged-marker, symlink, HOME and custom-parent refusals. Stub-browser tests: a silent browser honors a 1.5s timeout; an immediately exiting browser reports profile-in-use.
review_fixes: PR #2310 review: CDP moved from a DevTools TCP port to --remote-debugging-pipe (auth_browser_cdp.go, auth_browser_launch_pipe.go; Windows fallback auth_browser_launch_windows.go binds 127.0.0.1 with a random port, residual risk documented). The login profile is created 0700 with a marker file; --reset-profile deletes only a real (non-symlink) directory carrying that exact marker and refuses anything else, including a custom --login-profile-dir or its parent and HOME. Second review round: startLoginBrowser takes the login context and returns the exit channel, so a short --timeout or an early browser exit ends the wait (the Windows port-file wait included); browser stdio goes to the null device so Wait never blocks on a child holding an inherited pipe. User report follow-up (2026-10-14): the no-page-target check is debounced over browserClosedGrace (4s) so SSO redirects do not end the login, and the closed error names the last page seen with scheme, host and path only. PR #2319 review: when the browser process exits, the closed error also names the last page seen (no grace delay on that path).
